keyTakeaways: The Tamil Lexicon defines Deepavali as a pre-dawn festival on the 14th day of the waning moon in Aippasi, ordained by Krishna at Narakasura's request.
Tamil Deepavali 2027 is Thursday 28 October by Drik Panchang, a day before North India's Friday 29 October; one holiday calendar prints 29 October as an estimate.
In 2018 the split happened before: Tamil Nadu's G.O.Ms.No.937 put Deepavali on Tuesday 6 November, the central list on Wednesday 7 November.
On Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89, the nearest analogue), 27.0% of SubhSandesh greeting pages were built the day before; for a Tamil dawn greeting, that is the group that arrives in time.

faqs.question: Why does South India celebrate Deepavali on a different day?
faqs.answer: Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka by the same rule according to Drik Panchang, keep Deepavali on the morning when the Chaturdashi tithi is running before sunrise, while most of North India keeps it on the evening when Amavasya is running after sunset. In years when Chaturdashi ends before the next dawn, the Tamil day comes first, as it did on 6 November 2018 and will on Thursday 28 October 2027 by Drik Panchang's reckoning.

faqs.question: Which day should I take leave for Deepavali 2027 if my family is in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.answer: Take Thursday 28 October 2027, the morning of the oil bath by Drik Panchang's reckoning, and travel on Wednesday evening. Friday 29 October is the central gazetted Diwali holiday; the state's own 2027 order was not out as of 22 October 2026, and one holiday calendar prints 29 October as an estimate.

faqs.question: What is the story behind Deepavali in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.answer: It marks Narakasura's death at the hands of Krishna, with Satyabhama at his side in the popular Tamil telling. The Tamil Lexicon adds that Krishna ordained the festival at Narakasura's own request, which is why the day is kept with a bath and lamps rather than as a homecoming.

faqs.question: What is Ganga snanam on Deepavali?
faqs.answer: Ganga snanam is the oil bath taken before sunrise on Deepavali morning, named for the belief that water that dawn is as purifying as the Ganges. The Tamil Lexicon lists kaṅkā-snāṉam with the local sense 'oil-bath on the dīpāvaḷi day'.

faqs.question: What is Deepavali lehiyam and when is it eaten?
faqs.answer: Deepavali lehiyam, or Deepavali marundhu, is a thick paste usually made with dry ginger, pepper, ajwain, jaggery and ghee, eaten by the spoonful after the morning bath and before the sweets. Recipes vary by family, and we found no clinical study of it, so treat it as tradition rather than medicine.

faqs.question: What is Thala Deepavali?
faqs.answer: Thala Deepavali (talai tīpāvaḷi) is a newly married couple's first Deepavali, traditionally spent at the bride's parents' home with new clothes and the son-in-law's first Ganga snanam there. In 2027 that dawn is Thursday 28 October, so working couples should plan leave for Thursday and travel on Wednesday evening.

faqs.question: Do Tamil people do Lakshmi Puja on Deepavali?
faqs.answer: Many Tamil homes do a puja after the morning bath, but an evening Lakshmi Puja on Amavasya is a family choice in Tamil Nadu rather than the defining rite. Some women also keep Kedara Gowri vratham, which the Tamil Lexicon places on the same Aippasi Chaturdashi.

faqs.question: Does everyone in Tamil Nadu celebrate Deepavali?
faqs.answer: No. Thurston and Rangachari recorded in 1909 that the Rakshasa sept of the Toreyas of Coimbatore and Salem did not celebrate Dipavali because it honours a rakshasa's death, and some Tamil families today do not keep it either. Ask before assuming.

faqs.question: How do you say Happy Deepavali in Tamil?
faqs.answer: On the morning itself, the spoken greeting is often a question: கங்கா ஸ்நானம் ஆச்சா? (Gaṅgā snāṉam āccā?), 'has your Ganga bath been done?'. For a newly married couple, write தலை தீபாவளி வாழ்த்துக்கள் (talai tīpāvaḷi vāḻttukkaḷ), 'wishes on your first Deepavali'.

faqs.question: When will the Tamil Nadu government announce the 2027 Deepavali holiday?
faqs.answer: Probably in November or December 2026. The 2018 list was notified by G.O.Ms.No.937 on 7 November 2017, so the state usually publishes the next year's holidays late in the year before.

faqs.question: Can I write a Tamil greeting on the SubhSandesh Diwali page?
faqs.answer: Every line on the Happy Diwali page is editable, so you can type a Tamil greeting into the wishes and the letter. We have not tested every Tamil font on every phone, so press Save, preview it on your own phone and then publish the private link the night before the bath.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Why Diwali Is Celebrated in Tamil Nadu Before Sunrise

Why Diwali is celebrated in Tamil Nadu comes down to a death and a request. The festival marks Krishna's killing of Narakasura, and the Tamil Lexicon records that Krishna ordained it at the dying asura's own plea, to be kept with an auspicious oil bath before dawn. That is why the main day is the Chaturdashi morning, which in 2027 falls on Thursday 28 October, a day before North India's Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October.

The early start changes when a greeting has to be ready. On Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival SubhSandesh holds data for (89 pages, so a rough guide), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the festival day itself and 27.0% the day before. For a family awake at 4 AM only the day-before group arrives in time; below are the Ganga snanam, the 2027 date question, Thala Deepavali and Tamil greetings.

## What the Tamil Lexicon says Deepavali is, and why that matters

Deepavali in Tamil Nadu is the pre-dawn celebration of Narakasura's death, on the 14th day of the waning moon in the Tamil month of Aippasi (October to November). The [Tamil Lexicon's entry for தீபாவளி (tīpāvaḷi)](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%AA%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%B3%E0%AE%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact), compiled by the University of Madras in the 1920s and 1930s, says the festival is held at moonrise on that night and was ordained by Krishna at Narakasura's request.

That line explains what a North Indian visitor notices in a Madurai home. The day marks a demon's end, not a king's homecoming, so nobody waits for dusk; the household rises in the dark because that Chaturdashi moon comes up just before dawn.

It also answers a question children ask: why celebrate an asura's death at all? In this telling Narakasura asked that his last day be remembered with light, so the festival is his request granted, not only Krishna's victory.

## Ganga snanam at 4 AM: the oil bath, the question and the lehiyam

Ganga snanam is the Deepavali morning oil bath, and its name carries the belief that water on that dawn is as purifying as a dip in the Ganges. The Lexicon's supplement lists [கங்காஸ்நானம் (kaṅkā-snāṉam)](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%95%E0%AE%99%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%95%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B8%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A8%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%A9%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%8D&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) with a second, local sense: "oil-bath on the dīpāvaḷi day".

In most homes the order barely changes. An elder places warm nallennai (gingelly oil) on each person's head, and it comes off with shikakai in hot water before sunrise. New clothes follow, often with a dab of turmeric on the hem, then prayer, sweets and the first crackers.

The question every relative asks that morning is about the bath. "Ganga snanam aacha?" (has the Ganga bath been done?) works as the greeting itself, and the Lexicon's own example sentence under மங்களஸ்நானம் (maṅkaḷa-snāṉam, auspicious bath) is the same question in older Tamil.

Deepavali lehiyam, also called Deepavali marundhu (medicine), comes straight after: a dark, sticky paste usually built on dry ginger, pepper, ajwain, jaggery and ghee, taken by the spoonful before a day of murukku and adhirasam. The Lexicon defines lēkiyam simply as an electuary, a medicine eaten by licking. We found no clinical study of the Deepavali recipe, so read it as custom, not a health claim.

## Why Tamil Nadu's Deepavali can come a day early: the 2018 precedent

Tamil Nadu's Deepavali moves a day ahead of North India's whenever the Chaturdashi tithi is running at dawn but ends before the next evening. [Drik Panchang's 2027 Tamil Deepavali page](https://www.drikpanchang.com/tamil/festivals/tamil-deepavali/tamil-deepavali-date-time.html?year=2027) states the rule: most of India keeps Deepavali when Amavasya prevails just after sunset, while Tamil Nadu keeps it when Chaturdashi prevails just before sunrise, so the Tamil day may fall one day earlier or on the same day.

In 2018 the two rules split, and the state followed the dawn. Tamil Nadu's holiday order for that year, [G.O.Ms.No.937 of 7 November 2017](https://gconnect.in/news/tamil-nadu-state-government-holiday-list-2018.html), listed Deepavali on Tuesday 6 November 2018. The [Government of India's 2018 holiday memorandum of 14 June 2017](https://www.staffnews.in/2017/06/holidays-to-be-observed-in-central-2.html) put Diwali on Wednesday 7 November, listed "Deepavali (South India)" on 6 November as a restricted holiday, and let central offices close on Naraka Chaturdasi instead wherever a state declared only that day.

## Deepavali 2027 in Tamil Nadu: Thursday 28 or Friday 29 October?

By the pre-dawn rule, Tamil Deepavali 2027 is Thursday 28 October. Drik Panchang gives the Chaturdashi (Sathuradasi) tithi from 10:49 PM on 27 October to 8:47 PM on 28 October 2027, so it is running at Thursday's dawn and over by Friday's, and the same page lists North India's Deepavali on Friday 29 October.

Holiday calendars disagree as of 22 October 2026. Publicholidays.in lists Tamil Nadu's Deepavali on Friday 29 October 2027 and labels its whole 2027 table an estimate. The state government had not issued its 2027 order when this was written; the 2018 list was notified on 7 November 2017, so expect the 2027 order around November or December 2026.

Our reading: if Tamil Nadu repeats 2018, Thursday 28 October will be the state holiday. That is an inference from one precedent, not a notification, so do not book non-refundable travel on it.

The table sets the two calendars side by side. The last column carries the SubhSandesh figure behind each greeting decision.

| 2027 | Tamil Nadu | Most of North India | What it means for a greeting (SubhSandesh data) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main day | Thu 28 Oct, before sunrise | Fri 29 Oct, after sunset | 27.0% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built the day before; be in that group for a Tamil family |
| Tithi tested | Chaturdashi at dawn | Amavasya at dusk | 49.4% were built on the day itself, which works for the north, not for a 4 AM bath |
| Defining rite | Ganga snanam (oil bath) | Lakshmi Puja | 48.3% of shared pages open on a phone, the device beside the bathroom door |
| 2018 holiday | Tue 6 Nov (state G.O.) | Wed 7 Nov (central list) | Average page opened 11.1 times, so a link sent the night before still gets reopened |

The takeaway is simple. For Tamil Nadu, "on the day" means the night before.

## Thala Deepavali: a couple's first Deepavali, and why 2027 needs leave

Thala Deepavali (தலை தீபாவளி, talai tīpāvaḷi) is a newly married couple's first Deepavali, traditionally spent at the bride's parents' home. Thalai means head, and by extension first. The couple usually arrive the evening before, so that the son-in-law's first Ganga snanam in that house happens at dawn, often with the bride's parents placing the oil.

The bride's family dresses the couple in new clothes, and many mark the son-in-law's place with a gift that varies too much by community to quote a fair figure. In 2027 the Thala Deepavali dawn is Thursday 28 October, a working day on the central list, so a couple employed outside Tamil Nadu needs Thursday off and a Wednesday evening train or flight.

Sometimes only one of you can make that trip. If your spouse goes ahead while you are stuck at a desk in Pune, a private [I love you page for your partner](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) says what a forwarded card cannot; it is SubhSandesh's third most-made page, with 1,182 created by 24 September 2026.

## Kedara Gowri vratham, and the families that skip Deepavali

Not every Tamil home keeps the same morning. The Tamil Lexicon records Kedara Gowri vratham (கேதாரகௌரிவிரதம், kētāra-kauri-viratam), a vow kept by women on the Aippasi Krishna Chaturdashi in honour of Parvati of Kedaram, the same date as Deepavali. Families differ on whether the nonbu (vow) is kept that day or on the new moon after it, so follow your household's practice for 2027.

Some communities did not celebrate the day at all. Edgar Thurston and K. Rangachari's [Castes and Tribes of Southern India, volume 7 (1909)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/42997) records that among the Toreyas of Coimbatore and Salem, members of the Rakshasa sept did not celebrate Dipavali, because it honours "the victory over, and death of, a rakshasa".

It is a one-line entry, but it shows the Narakasura story was never neutral in Tamil country. For a lineage named after the losing side it was a reason to stay home, so a respectful greeting does not assume every Tamil friend keeps the day.

## Deepavali wishes in Tamil, with script and transliteration

Two lines Tamil speakers use come first, then two we wrote. Each word was checked against the Tamil Lexicon or Tamil Wiktionary.

- **கங்கா ஸ்நானம் ஆச்சா?** (Gaṅgā snāṉam āccā?) "Has your Ganga bath been done?" The dawn greeting, between people who will see each other that day.
- **தலை தீபாவளி வாழ்த்துக்கள்** (Talai tīpāvaḷi vāḻttukkaḷ) "Wishes on your first Deepavali." For a newly married couple.
- **உங்கள் வீட்டில் இந்த தீபாவளி ஒளியும் இனிமையும் நிறைக்கட்டும்** (Uṅkaḷ vīṭṭil inta tīpāvaḷi oḷiyum iṉimaiyum niṟaikkaṭṭum) "May this Deepavali fill your home with light and sweetness." Original.
- **இந்த வருடம் உங்கள் கையால் எண்ணெய் தேய்த்துக்கொள்ள வர முடியவில்லை; அடுத்த தீபாவளிக்கு வீட்டில் இருப்பேன்** (Inta varuṭam uṅkaḷ kaiyāl eṇṇey tēyttukkoḷḷa vara muṭiyavillai; aṭutta tīpāvaḷikku vīṭṭil iruppēn) "I couldn't come for the oil from your hands this year; next Deepavali I will be home." Original, for parents.

For one person you cannot reach at dawn, SubhSandesh's [interactive Happy Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) lets them light a diya at their door, wish diyas and sky lanterns holding up to six photos, then open your letter from a red-and-gold shagun liffafa. Every line is editable, so the Tamil can go in the letter; we have not tested every Tamil font on every phone, so preview first. Build it on Wednesday 27 October and send it that night.

## When a greeting link is the wrong Deepavali gesture in Tamil Nadu

A link loses to a phone call on the Ganga snanam morning. The elder who asks "Ganga snanam aacha?" wants to hear the answer, and a grandparent without a smartphone gets nothing from a page that 48.3% of viewers open on a phone. For Thala Deepavali the in-laws expect the couple in person, and a page sent instead reads as an excuse.

The Diwali page also leans North Indian by default: its closing card says Shubh Deepavali and its suggested songs include Aayee Hai Diwali. For a Tamil household you will replace the defaults with your own lines and perhaps a Tamil song from YouTube, and if that sounds like more work than a call, make the call.

failed.item: At least 1 of those is peer-reviewed or scholarly, and open-access
failed.why: No peer-reviewed open-access paper is cited. The scholarly sources are the University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (a scholarly dictionary) and Thurston and Rangachari's 1909 ethnography (a public-domain primary text, which BRIEF §5 accepts for ritual posts). Searched Crossref/Europe PMC via findpapers.mjs for 'Deepavali oil bath Tamil Nadu', 'Siddha medicine oil bath ennai kuliyal', 'Narakasura Deepavali Dravidian festival Tamil' and 'Siddha lehyam polyherbal digestive dry ginger': Europe PMC returned nothing open-access; the only on-topic hit (Rathinam et al. 2022, 'Significance of Siddha traditional oil bath (ennaimuzhukku)', Drug Combination Therapy, TMR Publishing, 2-page review) was read but not cited because the post makes no health claim it would support. Closes if an open-access study of Tamil Deepavali practice or the Naraka Chaturdashi oil bath is found.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the five pages analysed: it is the only one quoting a scholarly definition of Tamil Deepavali (Narakasura's request, Tamil Lexicon), the only one with a dated government precedent (TN 6 Nov vs central 7 Nov 2018) for the 2027 split, and the only one with Tamil-script greetings and a first-party timing figure. It cannot overcome the authority of Wikipedia and the state tourism site, and its first-party numbers are a Raksha Bandhan analogue, not Deepavali data; expect months, not weeks, and only for the long-tail 'why' phrasing.

structuralLimitations: BRIEF §1/§9 TN conflict confirmed: Drik Panchang (Tamil Deepavali page) gives Thu 28 Oct 2027; publicholidays.in lists Tamil Nadu Deepavali on Fri 29 Oct 2027 and labels its 2027 table an estimate. No official TN 2027 holiday G.O. found as of 2026-10-22. Post states the conflict, adds the 2018 precedent, and labels its 28 Oct reading an inference.

Cannibalisation gate vs anchor diwali-2027-date: 0 shared top-10 URLs. Sibling overlap avoided: choti-diwali-2027 already covers Chennai bath times, the Vishnu Purana story and the Drik tamil-festivals rule; this post cites a different Drik page (Tamil Deepavali date page) and adds Ganga snanam, lehiyam, Thala Deepavali, Kedara Gowri, the Toreya exception and the 2018 G.O.

happy-diwali-in-different-languages already cites the Tamil Lexicon தீபாவளி entry (for the dawn bath and the -கள்/-க்கள் spelling). This post reuses that dictionary URL (dsal is cap-exempt) for a different sense, the 'request of Narakasura' clause, and avoids its greeting line and spelling discussion.

Kedara Gowri vratham date: the Tamil Lexicon places it on the Aippasi Krishna Chaturdashi; current practice in some families is the following Amavasya. Not resolved from a citable source, so the post tells readers to follow household practice rather than printing a 2027 date.

Thala Deepavali customs (arrival the evening before, in-laws applying the oil) are stated as common practice with 'usually'/'often'; no citable ethnography for them was found. Tourism and hotel pages that mention Thala Deepavali rank top 5 and were not cited.

Drik Panchang's 2018 Diwali calendar returned a reCAPTCHA wall, so the 2018 split is sourced from the government lists (TN G.O. via GConnect, DoPT O.M. via StaffNews), not a panchang. Both are secondary reproductions of the orders; the original PDFs were not fetched.

Tamil greetings: 'Ganga snanam aacha?' is attested indirectly (Lexicon example under மங்களஸ்நானம்: 'இன்று மங்களஸ்நான மாயிற்றா?'); the two original Tamil lines were composed for this post and word-checked (ஒளி, இனிமை, எண்ணெய், வாழ்த்து) but not reviewed by a native editor.
